Suppose $U$ is a symmetric $[0,1]$-valued kernel on a finite probability space, $\mu=\mathbb EU>0$, and $$\tau=t(H,U),\qquad \Delta=\mu^{66}-\tau>0.$$ For any integer $$n>\frac{595+66\mu^{66}}{\Delta},
 \label{eq:kernel-host-size}$$ there is a finite simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}$.

The complex has the following properties.*

1.  *Every pair in $E$ lies in exactly two faces, $|E|=33$, and the face-neighbor graph is connected.*

2.  *For each bit position, each of its two classes consists of $11$ faces covering all $13$ points. Each class has an ordering in which every face after the first shares a pair with an earlier face and introduces exactly one new point.*

3.  *Every $a_e$ is at least $1/3$, and some $a_e$ is greater than $1/3$.*

4.  *Color refinement of $H$, starting with a separate color for each part, eventually gives distinct colors to all vertices within either part.

At the identity type assignments $a(i)=i$, $b(j)=j$, the sum in Equation [eq:kernel-coefficient] for the base laws has exactly one nonzero term. Its labels and value are $$\alpha_e=U_e\quad(e\in E),\qquad C_{A^{\mathrm{base}}}(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}) =-(\theta/2)^{66}. \label{eq:kernel-negative-term}$$
Assuming Lemma 5, there is a symmetric kernel $U:\Omega\times\Omega\to[0,1]$ on a finite probability space with mean $\mu>0$ such that $$t(H,U)<\mu^{66}. \label{eq:kernel-symmetric-gap}$$

Suppose $U$ is a symmetric $[0,1]$-valued kernel on a finite probability space, $\mu=\mathbb EU>0$, and $$\tau=t(H,U),\qquad \Delta=\mu^{66}-\tau>0.$$ For any integer $$n>\frac{595+66\mu^{66}}{\Delta},
 \label{eq:kernel-host-size}$$ there is a finite simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}$.

Suppose $r>1$. For each face $j$, let $\mathcal T_j$ be the event that all three differences between its point matrices are nonsingular. Then, uniformly over the activity and sign choices, $$\label{eq:transverse-local-l1}
 \mathbb E\bigl[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T_j}|F_j-G_j|\bigr]=O(q^{-1/2}).$$ Moreover $0\leq F_j\leq C_D$ on $\mathcal T_j$, for a constant $C_D$ independent of $q$, and $0\leq G_j\leq8$ everywhere.
For fixed even $D\geq12$, the law of $(\eta_e^X)_{e\in E}$ converges in total variation to that of independent uniform signs on $\{+1,-1\}^E$.

In a symplectic $2N$-space, the following formulas hold.*

1.  *The number of Lagrangians is $L_N$.*


2.  *A fixed isotropic $t$-space is contained in exactly $L_{N-t}$ Lagrangians. Consequently its containment probability and the number of isotropic $t$-spaces are, respectively, $$\vartheta_N(t)=\frac{L_{N-t}}{L_N},\qquad
     I_N(t)=\frac{L_N}{L_{N-t}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{N}{t}_q.
     \label{eq:orbits-containment}$$*


3.  *For a fixed Lagrangian $A$, the number of Lagrangians $B$ with $\dim(A\cap B)=h$ is $\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{N}{h}_q q^{b(N-h)}$. Thus $$\pi_{N,h}:=\mathbb P\{\dim(A\cap B)=h\}
     =\frac{\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{N}{h}_q q^{b(N-h)}}{L_N}.
     \label{eq:orbits-pair-probability}$$ All ordered pairs with the same intersection dimension belong to one symplectic orbit.*

*For fixed $N$, these formulas give $$\begin{aligned}
 L_N&=(1+O_N(q^{-1}))q^{b(N)},
 &\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{t}_q&=(1+O_n(q^{-1}))q^{t(n-t)},\\
 \vartheta_N(t)&\asymp_N q^{-Nt+\binom t2},
 &I_N(t)&\asymp_N q^{2Nt-(3t^2-t)/2},\\
 \pi_{N,h}&\asymp_N q^{-b(h)}.
 \label{eq:orbits-count-exponents}
\end{aligned}$$

For three independent uniform Lagrangians, every feasible dimensional profile has probability $O_D(q^{-C})$. More strongly, there is a constant $\kappa_D>0$, independent of $q$ and of the particular orbit, such that for every occurring ordered symplectic orbit $\mathcal O$ of that profile, $$\kappa_D q^{-C}\le
 \mathbb P\{(L_1,L_2,L_3)\in\mathcal O\}
 \le \kappa_D^{-1}q^{-C}.
 \label{eq:orbits-orbit-mass}$$ The constant can be chosen for all odd primes. Moreover, conditional on any fixed ordered pair having intersection dimension $h$, the probability that an independent third Lagrangian completes a specified dimensional profile is $$O_D(q^{-C+b(h)}).
 \label{eq:orbits-conditional-profile}$$

For three independent uniform $r'$-subspaces of a $d$-space, the event of common intersection zero, opposite pair dimensions $p_i$, and span codimension $v$ has probability $$\label{eq:planted-subspace-cost}
 O\left(q^{-\delta P-\sum_i p_i^2-vw}\right).$$
Every tuple satisfying Equation [eq:tail-feasible] satisfies $$\label{eq:coercivity} Q\ge\frac1{342}(P^2+T^2+\delta^2).$$

Let $H_e$ be subspaces assigned to distinct pairs $e$ of a simple graph. Set $$k=\dim\sum_e H_e,\qquad k_i=\dim\sum_{e\ni i}H_e.$$ Then $\sum_i k_i\ge2k$. If the nonzero spaces do not form a direct sum, then $\sum_i k_i\ge2k+1$.

For a profile satisfying Equation [eq:tail-residual-profile], let $m$ be the number of pairs with $h_e=2$. The contribution of configurations whose pair spaces are not direct is $O_D(q^{-D+1641})$. The contribution of configurations whose pair spaces are direct is $$O_D\left(q^{-\frac13\sum_e b(h_e)}\right).$$ Here “contribution” includes the product of the center factors. The numerical remainder $1641$ is independent of $D$.

coverage.checked_domain: The listed valid integer inputs, including h=0, odd h, even h and h=2*r. For each input the oracle exhaustively enumerates every admissible p,t pair.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact enumeration of the original objective under p+t=h and 0<=t<=p<=r, independently of the closed form. Agreement on these finite vectors does not prove the identity for all dimensions.
